items.stem: ‘Slavery was the main cause of sectional tension in the United States between 1820 and 1840.’ How far do you agree?
items.answer: For: The Missouri crisis was about the expansion of slavery. Abolitionism after 1831 alarmed the South. The gag rule showed slavery could not be discussed calmly. Against: The tariff and the nullification crisis set the South against northern economic interests. Disputes over federal power and states' rights were constitutional. In the 1830s party loyalties to Whigs and Democrats cut across sections. Judgement: slavery lay behind most disputes, but before 1840 the two-party system and compromise kept sectional tension under control.

items.stem: ‘The Compromise of 1850 settled the issue of slavery in the territories.’ Discuss.
items.answer: For: It admitted California as free and left Utah and New Mexico to popular sovereignty. It calmed the crisis of 1849-50 and secession talk died down. Both main parties accepted it as a final settlement in 1852. Against: The Fugitive Slave Act increased northern hostility to slavery. Popular sovereignty was vague and was soon extended to Kansas-Nebraska. It was an armistice rather than a compromise: no majority supported the whole package. Judgement: it ended the immediate crisis but settled nothing, because the principle of popular sovereignty reopened the question in 1854.

items.stem: To what extent did westward expansion cause the growth of sectional conflict between 1845 and 1850?
items.answer: For: The Mexican War added territory whose status divided the sections. The Wilmot Proviso split Congress on sectional lines. California's statehood threatened the balance in the Senate. Against: Slavery itself, and moral opposition to it, was the deeper cause. Abolitionism and fugitive slave cases raised tension independently. Political leaders reached compromise in 1850, showing expansion need not cause conflict. Judgement: expansion was the main trigger of conflict in these years because it turned slavery into a question about the future of the West.

items.stem: The Kansas-Nebraska Act of 1854 allowed settlers in those territories to decide on slavery by popular sovereignty. ‘The Kansas-Nebraska Act was the most important cause of the rise of the Republican Party.’ Discuss.
items.answer: For: It reopened the issue of slavery in territory closed to it since 1820. It led directly to the founding of the party in 1854. Bleeding Kansas kept the issue alive. Against: The collapse of the Whig Party left voters looking for a new party. Nativism and the decline of the Know-Nothings brought in voters. Dred Scott and the Lecompton constitution deepened fears of the Slave Power. The free labour ideology had wide appeal. Judgement: Kansas-Nebraska was the trigger and the most important single cause, but the party became a major force because the Whigs collapsed and later events confirmed fears of the Slave Power.

items.stem: What is meant by “Manifest Destiny”?
options: The government formed by the seceded states in February 1861, with Jefferson Davis as president.
The northern belief that a conspiracy of slaveholders controlled the federal government.
Loyalty to the interests of one region (North, South or West) above those of the nation.
The belief that the United States was destined to expand across the North American continent.
items.answer: The belief that the United States was destined to expand across the North American continent.
items.markingKey: Manifest Destiny: the belief that the United States was destined to expand across the North American continent. [1]

items.stem: Explain why the Mexican War increased sectional tension.
items.answer: It raised the question of slavery in the new territories. The Wilmot Proviso divided Congress on sectional lines. Many northerners saw it as a war to extend slavery. Gold in California made a decision urgent. Judgement: by adding vast new territory, the war forced the question of slavery's expansion back into national politics.

items.stem: Historians have offered several reasons why the Compromise of 1850 was agreed. A: The death of President Taylor removed an obstacle and Fillmore supported it. B: California's application for statehood forced a decision. C: Douglas passed the measures as separate bills with different majorities. Explain how these reasons were linked and decide which mattered most.
items.answer: Any reasoned choice. A: The death of President Taylor removed an obstacle and Fillmore supported it. B: California's application for statehood forced a decision. C: Douglas passed the measures as separate bills with different majorities. Possible judgement: it was passed through political skill rather than genuine agreement, as each measure had a different majority.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for a choice; up to 3 marks for explaining it with precise detail; up to 2 marks for comparing it with the other reasons [6]

items.stem: Put these events in chronological order, starting with the earliest. A: The Kansas-Nebraska Act was passed. B: John Brown raided Harpers Ferry. C: The Supreme Court decided the Dred Scott case. D: Lincoln and Douglas held a series of debates in Illinois.
items.answer: A, C, D, B (A 1854; C March 1857; D 1858; B October 1859)

items.stem: Chloe is planning an answer to the question: “‘The Kansas-Nebraska Act was the most important cause of the rise of the Republican Party.’ How far do you agree?” Write a one-sentence line of argument for the answer and outline two points Chloe could use to support the view and two to challenge it.
items.answer: Line of argument: Kansas-Nebraska was the trigger and the most important single cause, but the party became a major force because the Whigs collapsed and later events confirmed fears of the Slave Power. Support: It reopened the issue of slavery in territory closed to it since 1820. It led directly to the founding of the party in 1854. Challenge: The collapse of the Whig Party left voters looking for a new party. Nativism and the decline of the Know-Nothings brought in voters.
items.markingKey: 2 marks for a line of argument that answers the question directly and is sustainable; 1 mark for each relevant supporting point and 1 for each challenging point [6]

items.stem: Consider the following explanations of why the Dred Scott decision increased sectional tension. A: It encouraged southern demands for federal protection of slavery in the territories. B: Northerners saw it as proof of a Slave Power conspiracy. C: It declared the Missouri Compromise unconstitutional. Explain how these reasons were linked and decide which mattered most.
items.answer: Any reasoned choice. A: It encouraged southern demands for federal protection of slavery in the territories. B: Northerners saw it as proof of a Slave Power conspiracy. C: It declared the Missouri Compromise unconstitutional. Possible judgement: it raised tension by making compromise impossible: the Republican programme was declared unconstitutional.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for a choice; up to 3 marks for explaining it with precise detail; up to 2 marks for comparing it with the other reasons [6]

items.stem: A student writes: “Lincoln promised in 1860 to abolish slavery in the southern states.” Is this accurate? Explain your answer using your own knowledge.
items.answer: Not accurate. He opposed the expansion of slavery but said he had no intention of interfering with it where it existed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for a correct judgement; 1 mark for accurate supporting knowledge [2]

items.stem: Explain one reason why the Deep South seceded after Lincoln's election.
items.answer: Southerners feared a Republican president would threaten slavery in the long term.
items.markingKey: For each reason: 1 mark for identifying it and 1 mark for explaining it with supporting detail, from: Southerners feared a Republican president would threaten slavery in the long term. Lincoln had won without any southern votes, showing the South had lost power in the Union. Fire-eaters had prepared opinion for secession. John Brown's raid had increased fears of slave rebellion. They believed in the right of states to leave the Union. [2]

items.stem: Consider the following explanations of why attempts at compromise failed in 1860-61. A: Lincoln and the Republicans refused to allow slavery to expand into the territories. B: Buchanan was weak and did little. C: Secessionists did not want compromise. Which was the most significant? Explain your answer with reference to the other reasons.
items.answer: Any reasoned choice. A: Lincoln and the Republicans refused to allow slavery to expand into the territories. B: Buchanan was weak and did little. C: Secessionists did not want compromise. Possible judgement: compromise failed because the one issue that mattered, the expansion of slavery, was the one neither side would give way on.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for a choice; up to 3 marks for explaining it with precise detail; up to 2 marks for comparing it with the other reasons [6]

items.stem: In November 1860 Lincoln won the presidency without carrying a single state in the Deep South. How far was Lincoln responsible for the outbreak of war in 1861?
items.answer: For: He refused to accept the Crittenden Compromise. He decided to resupply Fort Sumter. His call for 75,000 volunteers drove the upper South to secede. Against: The Deep South seceded before he took office. The Confederacy fired the first shots. He tried to avoid provocation, sending only food to Sumter. Judgement: Lincoln was determined to preserve the Union, but responsibility for the outbreak lies mainly with the secessionists who left before he took office and fired first.

items.stem: How successful was the Missouri Compromise in reducing sectional conflict?
items.answer: For: It kept the balance in the Senate. It settled the status of slavery in the Louisiana Purchase for over thirty years. No major crisis over territory followed until the 1840s. Against: It drew a geographical line that encouraged sectional thinking. It did not settle the question of slavery in future territories. Jefferson called it a "fire bell in the night", warning of future conflict. Judgement: it was successful in the short and medium term, but it postponed rather than solved the problem of slavery in the West.

items.stem: What is meant by “Wilmot Proviso”?

The party formed in 1848 to oppose the spread of slavery into the western territories.
The northern belief that a conspiracy of slaveholders controlled the federal government.
The government formed by the seceded states in February 1861, with Jefferson Davis as president.

items.stem: Ethan is planning an answer to the question: “‘The Compromise of 1850 settled the issue of slavery in the territories.’ How far do you agree?” Write a one-sentence line of argument for the answer and outline two points Ethan could use to support the view and two to challenge it.
items.answer: Line of argument: it ended the immediate crisis but settled nothing, because the principle of popular sovereignty reopened the question in 1854. Support: It admitted California as free and left Utah and New Mexico to popular sovereignty. It calmed the crisis of 1849-50 and secession talk died down. Challenge: The Fugitive Slave Act increased northern hostility to slavery. Popular sovereignty was vague and was soon extended to Kansas-Nebraska.
items.markingKey: 2 marks for a line of argument that answers the question directly and is sustainable; 1 mark for each relevant supporting point and 1 for each challenging point [6]

items.stem: A student writes: “The Kansas-Nebraska Act banned slavery in Kansas.” Is this accurate? Explain your answer using your own knowledge.
items.answer: Not accurate. It left the decision to the settlers through popular sovereignty.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for a correct judgement; 1 mark for accurate supporting knowledge [2]

items.stem: Priya is planning an answer to the question: “To what extent was the breakdown of the second party system responsible for the sectional crisis of the 1850s?” Write a one-sentence line of argument for the answer and outline two points Priya could use to support the view and two to challenge it.
items.answer: Line of argument: the collapse of national parties made the crisis much harder to manage, but slavery was the issue that broke them. Support: The collapse of the Whigs ended a national party that had bridged the sections. Sectional parties made compromise harder. Challenge: Slavery was the issue that caused the parties to break down. Events such as Kansas, Dred Scott and Harpers Ferry polarised opinion.
items.markingKey: 2 marks for a line of argument that answers the question directly and is sustainable; 1 mark for each relevant supporting point and 1 for each challenging point [6]

items.stem: Read Source D. “A house divided against itself cannot stand. items.answer: Reliable because it is Lincoln's own words at the time. Less reliable because it was a campaign speech intended to win votes and define his difference from Douglas. items.stem: Grace is planning an answer to the question: “‘The southern states seceded mainly to protect slavery.’ How far do you agree?” Write a one-sentence line of argument for the answer and outline two points Grace could use to support the view and two to challenge it.

Support: The declarations of causes of states such as South Carolina and Mississippi stressed slavery. Fear of Republican hostility to slavery followed Lincoln's election. Challenge: Southerners argued for states' rights and constitutional liberty. Loss of political power in the Union alarmed southern leaders.

items.stem: Read the sources carefully. Source A: Alexander Stephens, vice-president of the Confederacy, "Cornerstone" speech, March 1861 (abridged). “Our new government is founded upon the great truth that the negro is not equal to the white man; that slavery, subordination to the superior race, is his natural and normal condition.” Source B: a speech by a southern Unionist, 1861 (illustrative). “We are told the North means to march armies against us. I will stand by Virginia; I did not want to leave the Union, but I will not fight my neighbours.” Source C: South Carolina's Declaration of the Immediate Causes of Secession, December 1860 (abridged). “An increasing hostility on the part of the non-slaveholding States to the institution of slavery has led to a disregard of their obligations.” “The southern states seceded mainly to protect slavery.” How far do Sources A, B and C support this view?
items.answer: Source A supports: it shows slavery as the cornerstone of the new nation. Evaluation: it was an improvised speech and Stephens later claimed it was misreported. Source B challenges: it suggests loyalty to the state and opposition to coercion. Evaluation: it is one person's view and illustrative. Source C supports: it names hostility to slavery as the reason for secession. Evaluation: it was written to justify a decision already made. Grouping: support A, C; challenge B. A judgement must weigh how convincing each group is, using provenance and own knowledge, rather than counting sources.

Level 2 (5-8): uses the sources to support OR challenge. Level 1 (1-4): writes about the topic without valid use of the sources.
